External releases

releases.Rd

A release is what the external source made available. Its form decides which divergences can use it (the divergence argument of cv.bregsurv()):

Usage

release_records(
  z,
  time = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  stratum = NULL,
  case = NULL,
  set = NULL,
  interval = NULL
)

release_coef(beta, Q = NULL)

release_score(score)

release_model(beta = NULL, baseline = NULL, hazard = NULL, Q = NULL)

Arguments

z

Covariates of the external records, with the target's column names.

time, event, stratum

External follow-up, event indicator and strata (cohort records).

case, set

External case indicator and matched sets (nested case-control records).

interval

External interval index (records for a discrete-time target).

beta

Named external coefficient vector. Every name must be one of your covariates; covariates the release does not cover are set to zero (see align_beta()).

Q

Optional precision matrix of beta (inverse covariance or information matrix), named like beta.

score

Numeric vector: the external risk score of each target subject.

baseline

Baseline cumulative-hazard increments of the external Cox model over the target's intervals 1, ..., K.

hazard

Matrix of external interval hazards, one row per target subject and one column per interval (an alternative to beta + baseline).

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_release".

Details

releasedivergences it supports
release_records(): individual-level recordscomposite likelihood; on a Cox target also Mahalanobis and Kullback-Leibler, through a Cox model fitted to the records
release_coef(): coefficients, optionally with their precision matrix QMahalanobis (Euclidean when Q = NULL) and Kullback-Leibler
release_score(): a risk score evaluated on your subjectsKullback-Leibler
release_model(): coefficients with the baseline hazard, or interval hazardsKullback-Leibler on the discrete-time target (absolute risk), and everything release_coef() supports

Examples

data(ExampleData_lowdim)
release_coef(ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_fair)
#> Release: 6 coefficients
